claims.claim: The opt-in transport fixes the model to gemini-3.8-flash, requires caller-supplied effort, and makes one read-only native process call confined to an isolated workspace. It does not register a Reviewer default or use Executor profile routing.

The transport writes the exact bounded request bytes to a fresh temporary workspace, copies its output schema there, removes the workspace after the call, and returns the existing JsonReviewerProvider wrapper for P3 semantic validation.

The parser fails closed on native process, envelope, output-bound, and usage-witness errors without a retry. Successful calls retain only a frozen observation containing the request digest, provider, model, effort, one-call count, and bounded usage counters.

The new test file defines deterministic injected-runner cases for isolation, bounds, cleanup, failure behavior, P3 composition, and fingerprint independence. The implementation changes only the three TASK-191 paths and contains no real provider invocation or BP-8 completion claim.
